subject: Chemistry
title: Polonium-210: The Spy's Poison
description: Learn Polonium-210: The Spy's Poison in one minute.

hook.text: In 2006, former Russian spy Alexander Litvinenko was killed by polonium-210 slipped into his tea in London.

buildup.text: Polonium-210 is intensely radioactive. It emits alpha particles that shred DNA and proteins inside cells.

discovery.text: Alpha particles can't penetrate skin from outside—but inside the body, they devastate organs at close range.

twist.text: It took three weeks for Litvinenko to die. Doctors couldn't identify the poison until it was too late.

climax.text: Police traced the polonium trail across London using Geiger counters. It left radioactive traces everywhere.

punchline.text: Invisible, tasteless, radioactive. The perfect assassination weapon left a glowing trail.

quiz.question: Why is polonium-210 so deadly when ingested?
options: Its alpha particles destroy DNA and proteins from inside the body
It reacts with stomach acid to produce toxic gas
It blocks the kidneys from filtering blood

details.summary: Polonium-210 is an intensely radioactive alpha emitter that was used to assassinate Russian dissident Alexander Litvinenko in London in 2006. Just micrograms are lethal because alpha particles devastate cells internally despite being stopped by skin externally.
details.whyItMatters: The Litvinenko case demonstrated that radioactive poisons can be weaponized for targeted assassination. It raised awareness of nuclear security and the dangers of uncontrolled radioisotope access.
takeaways: Polonium-210 emits alpha particles that destroy cells from inside
Microgram quantities are lethally radioactive when ingested
The Litvinenko assassination was traced through polonium trails

faq.question: Why was polonium-210 chosen as an assassination weapon?
faq.answer: Polonium-210 is nearly undetectable by standard toxicology screens and produces symptoms that initially resemble ordinary illness. Alpha radiation is invisible to Geiger counters behind even thin barriers. It required specialized nuclear forensics to identify the cause of death.

faq.question: How did investigators trace the polonium back to the assassins?
faq.answer: Polonium-210 leaves radioactive contamination on every surface it touches. Investigators traced contamination trails across London hotels, restaurants, planes, and offices, mapping the movements of the suspects and identifying the isotopic signature as Russian-produced.
